newsitem.title: USA: Senator to seek reversal of Mexican certification.
newsitem.headline: Senator to seek reversal of Mexican certification.

text.p: Sen. Dianne Feinstein said on Friday she would lead an effort in Congress to disapprove President Bill Clinton's decision to certify Mexico as a U.S. partner in the war on drugs.
"I now intend to work with my colleagues to prepare and submit a resolution to disapprove this decision in the Congress," Feinstein, a California Democrat, said in a statement.

Such a resolution would have to be passed by both the House of Representatives and the Senate and sent to Clinton. If the president vetoed it, as he almost certainly would, it would have to be passed again by a two-thirds majority in order to become effective.
Feinstein called the decision to certify Mexico, expected to be announced on Friday afternoon, a mistake.

"The law requires the president to certify that Mexico has 'cooperated fully with the United States, or taken adequate steps on its own' to combat drug trafficking. I do not see how such an assertion can be made," she said.

"Have we received some cooperation from Mexico? Undoubtedly. President Zeillo and many others are working with us in good faith. But have we received full cooperation? Not even close," Feinstein said.
